notes.text: This manuscript leaf has author number 3), a separate circled item 3, an opening replacement above a cancelled line, condition pair (12), a heavily revised NB, three lower marginal notes, a diagonal upper marginal definition, one unheaded marginal rule, and thin foliation 15. The full image and both supplied native halves were each inspected once, then all nineteen saved crops once. P09/P16/P17/P18 are rotated 45 degrees clockwise for readability; all boxes use original 1692×2365 coordinates. The main sequence occupies approximately twenty-five physical text/display rows, excluding raised and marginal additions. H’s page-order inference, explanatory comments, and supplied terminal ellipsis are editorial and are not source text.

The local mathematical content defines a conical subspace using (a) stability under interval homotheties and (b) a cone-neighborhood structure for the restricted operation. Its NB then asserts intrinsic-boundary and scaled-subspace intersection identities and describes such subspaces by a closed outer-boundary subset and a base subset containing its zero image. The upper margin calls the case with no extra base points strict. The final paragraphs define simultaneous compatibility with closed subspaces and a stronger compatibility involving an exterior cylindrical neighborhood. These descriptions are source summaries; the specific checks and failures are recorded separately below.

Independent radial-truncation counterexample to the two NB identities under the literal conditions (a),(b), using the interval-action mapping-cylinder definition supplied for this run. Take T=[0,1], Y={0}, with scalar action mu·t=mu t, and T-prime=[0,a] for 0<a<1. Condition (a) holds because 0≤mu t≤a for mu∈[0,1] and t∈[0,a]. The map h:[0,1]→[0,a], h(s)=as, is a homeomorphism fixing 0 and satisfies h(mu s)=mu h(s), so the restricted action on T-prime is again the absolute cone action. T-prime is also an ambient neighborhood of 0 in T because it contains [0,a), open relative to [0,1]. Thus the literal (b) is satisfied with the same Y={0}. But the intrinsic outer boundary of T-prime is {a}, whereas T-prime intersect dot T is [0,a] intersect {1}=empty. Also, for 0<lambda<1, lambda T-prime=[0,a lambda], whereas T-prime intersect T_lambda=[0,min(a,lambda)]. Taking a=lambda=1/2 gives [0,1/4] versus [0,1/2]. This refutes the implication from the printed local conditions alone to both NB identities. A stronger boundary-preserving, normalized-radius, or full-ambient-ray saturation convention could exclude this example, but such a condition is not present in (a),(b) as written. No source formula is repaired.

Targeted corrected-scope check of the reconstruction and strict correspondence. In a mapping cylinder C(f) of f:B→Y, write q for the quotient, with outer boundary B×{1}. For a closed subset A of B and a subspace C of Y satisfying f(A)⊂C, define S=q(A×[0,1]) union C. Then S has precisely A as its outer slice and C as its base intersection; it is invariant under the ambient scalar action. For every lambda∈[0,1], lambda S=C union q(A×[0,lambda]), and S intersect T_lambda is the same set. The source’s NB identities therefore hold for these full-ambient-ray saturated subcones. Conversely any such saturated S is uniquely determined by A=S intersect dot T and C=S intersect Y. Under the additional strict condition C=f(A), S is determined by A alone, proving the claimed closed-A/strict-subcone correspondence within this stronger class. The scalar-stable truncated example in N03 is not of this form. Closedness of A is retained as the source stipulates; it is not derived from conditions (a),(b) by this argument.

Independent topological check that the construction in N04 has the expected subspace topology when A is closed in B, without requiring C closed in Y. The natural continuous injection C(f restricted to A:A→C)→C(f) has image S. To prove it is an embedding, let F be closed in the smaller mapping cylinder. Its quotient preimages F_C⊂C and F_A⊂A×[0,1] are closed and compatible at zero. Extend F_C to a closed F_Y⊂Y with F_Y intersect C=F_C. Since A is closed in B, F_A is closed in B×[0,1]. The subset F_Y disjoint union (F_A union (f^{-1}(F_Y)×{0})) of Y disjoint union B×[0,1] is closed and saturated for the ambient quotient: zero-level membership agrees with F_Y, and compatibility of F_A at zero prevents an additional base identification. Its quotient image is closed in C(f), and its intersection with S is exactly F. Thus every closed set of the smaller cylinder is closed relative to S, which proves the embedding. This establishes the conditional construction used in N04, not the unrestricted classification asserted in the source NB.

Two separate base-variable diagnostics are preserved. First, condition (12)b ends in an unprimed Y, so read literally it makes T-prime a neighborhood of all of Y. The later classification permits a subspace Y-prime of Y containing only the zero image of the selected outer boundary. An arbitrary proper Y-prime need not contain all of Y.
